title: Settings: Keyboard Manager editor shortcut is triggered even after being cleared
author: jiripolasek
summary: Clearing a module hotkey restores its default registration instead of disabling it, so the old Keyboard Manager editor shortcut still fires and similar behavior may affect other modules.

confidence.rationale: The issue identifies the exact fallback mechanism, but shared settings semantics and current-version persistence require verification.

judgment.rationale: The issue author identified a concrete fallback in Keyboard Manager dllmain that substitutes the default hotkey when the configured value is empty. The expected clear-versus-reset semantics can be tested locally.
evidence: Clearing Win+Shift+Q does not stop the Keyboard Manager editor from opening.
The author points to dllmain.cpp logic that appears to restore the default when the hotkey is unassigned.
A commenter reports similar clear behavior in Color Picker and Mouse Jump.
judgment.recommended_action: Represent disabled/cleared hotkeys explicitly and avoid default fallback except during first-run or reset-to-default operations.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The code-level hypothesis is strong enough for a design candidate. The implementation should distinguish first-run defaulting, explicit reset, and explicit disable without breaking existing users' settings.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve explicitly cleared module hotkeys
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hotkey registration falls back to the module default when the configured shortcut is empty, treating an intentional clear as if configuration were absent.
plan: Add or reuse an explicit disabled-state representation that differs from missing/uninitialized settings.
Update Keyboard Manager hotkey registration to skip registration when the user explicitly clears the shortcut; reserve default fallback for first-run/reset.
Audit modules using the same pattern and add persistence/migration tests for default, custom, cleared, and reset states.
verification: Clear the Keyboard Manager editor shortcut, restart PowerToys, and confirm the former default no longer opens it.
Reset to default and verify the default registers again; repeat the state matrix for any shared modules changed.

issue_context.summary: Clearing a module hotkey restores its default registration instead of disabling it, so the old Keyboard Manager editor shortcut still fires and similar behavior may affect other modules.
known_information: The issue was filed from a PowerToys 0.98 development build.
Reassigning the hotkey to a different chord works around the problem.
No active linked fix exists; the cross-referenced PR 49511 belongs to a different Command Palette issue.
inferences: The settings model likely conflates missing/uninitialized configuration with an intentionally empty hotkey.
Other modules may share the same fallback convention and require a common migration rule.
